newsitem.title: BELGIUM: QUEST FOR "EUROPLUG" HITS FRESH SETBACK.
newsitem.headline: QUEST FOR "EUROPLUG" HITS FRESH SETBACK.

text.p: The quest for a common European power plug and socket has suffered a major setback, with national members of the electrical standards body that must devise the new system rejecting a draft plan.
The Brussels-based standards body Cenelec said a proposal to create a "Europlug" to replace the many different types of connectors across Europe had failed to receive the necessary majority.
"In the immediate future, therefore, there will be no European standards for a harmonised system," it said in a statement.
In April 1995 Cenelec members rejected an earlier proposal for a standardised system.
The proposal would have introduced a standard plug with two or three round pins to allow appliances to be used across Europe without adapters.
The European Commission, advocating a common system but not involved in the work of Cenelec, reacted with disappointment.
"Everybody says; 'by all means, have a Europlug but only mine is safe enough," one official at the European Union executive said.

A national official said it was not just a technical question, but rather an issue touching upon national industry and trade policy. By having a national system, the market is protected from competition, he said.

It was not clear how many of the 18 national standards bodies that make up its membership voted against the plan, but Britain has earlier opposed a standardised system because of safety concerns. Germany also voted no the last time.
